Triggers.value: Physical pain in a part of the body

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I worry obsessively about bad things happening to people I care about
rehearse what to say before any interaction

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I feel on guard even inside my own home
Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen

Memory.value: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it
I cannot tell a clear story of what happened even to myself
I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns

issues.explanation: For a 42-year-old woman whose trauma type is stalking, helicopter or aircraft sounds are hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The threat, memory, and maladaptive strategy items all describe hypervigilance, fragmented recall, and interpersonal avoidance consistent with stalking, but no other selected item suggests an aviation-related cue or context. This trigger appears clinically disconnected from the trauma type and from the strong Triggers→Threat / Triggers→Memory pattern in the formulation.

vignette: Lekha, a 42-year-old South Asian woman, has been working as a maid for over two decades. Her life took a dark turn when she was stalked by a man who would follow her home and make inappropriate sexual comments while lingering near her residence. The trauma of the stalking has left Lekha feeling vulnerable and constantly on edge. Lekha’s experiences during this time were marked by intense physical discomfort, often accompanied by the smell of alcohol that the stalker would emit as he followed her. These triggers continue to be potent reminders of the threat she faced; even a casual look from someone or the scent of alcohol now sets off waves of anxiety and fear within her. Her husband noticed early on that Lekha had become extremely vigilant, repeatedly checking that all doors and windows were locked every night. Inside her home, Lekha felt like she was under constant surveillance, always alert for any unusual sounds or movements. The silence in the house would often make her feel as though something dangerous was about to happen, reinforcing her sense of threat. Lekha’s memories of the stalking are fragmented and incomplete; she finds herself pushing away thoughts before they fully surface. This inability to form a coherent narrative of what happened makes it difficult for her to process and understand her trauma. When fragments do return, Lekha can vividly taste the sourness in her mouth from the stress she experienced during those moments. The vivid nature of these memories often leads to catastrophizing; Lekha worries obsessively about bad things happening to people she cares about. She rehearses conversations in her head before speaking with anyone, fearing that a single misstep could trigger another threatening encounter. This heightened state of anxiety has led her to avoid seeing friends and social gatherings altogether. As time passed, the memory of being stalked became entangled with her sense of threat, making it difficult for Lekha to feel safe in any environment. She would often find herself hyperaware of her surroundings, constantly scanning for signs of danger. This cycle of fear led to a reinforcing loop where each trigger and memory activated deeper layers of anxiety. The impact on her daily life was significant; Lekha’s work as a maid became fraught with difficulties. Simple tasks were marred by constant interruptions as she would pause to check her surroundings or re-experience the trauma through sensory triggers. Her husband observed that she often came home exhausted and distressed, unable to shake off the lingering sense of danger. Lekha finally decided to seek help when she realized that her avoidance behaviors were beginning to isolate her from friends and family. What frightened her most was not just the ongoing threat but the growing isolation and the fear that she might never feel safe again. She hopes therapy will provide a way for her to process her trauma, regain some sense of normalcy in her daily life, and reconnect with the world around her without being consumed by constant fear.
